R.DEVDAS J., (ORAL):
The petitioner is seeking to quash the impugned notification dated 19.12.1998, issued under Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

2. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned notification has been subject matter of various litigations and this Court has allowed all the writ petitions and has quashed the impugned notification, insofar as the respective writ petitioners are concerned.
Learned Counsel prays for similar orders, having regard to the decision in the case of Sri.C.Valliappa Vs. The State of Karnataka and others, in W.P.No.8400/2021, dated 07.06.2021.

entities.text: Sri.C.Valliappa Vs. The State of Karnataka and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned Counsel appearing for the respondent- Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB) and learned Counsel appearing for the respondent-Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprises (NICE), do not dispute the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the petitioner.

However, the learned Counsel for the respondent No.4-NICE would draw the attention of this Court to another NC: 2023:KHC:28596 decision in the case of Sri.Natawarlal Jasu Vs. The State of Karnataka and others, in W.P.No.4399/2023, dated 28.07.2023 and prays that similar directions that were issued to the respondent-State Government and liberty granted to the respondent-NICE,
may be given.
4.

entities.text: Sri.Natawarlal Jasu Vs. The State of Karnataka and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the decisions of the co-ordinate Benches of this Court striking down the impugned notification, the petitioner is also entitled for similar relief.
5. Consequently, the writ petition is allowed.

The impugned preliminary notification dated 19.12.1998 issued under Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966, is hereby quashed and set aside, insofar as the petitioner's lands i.e., schedule properties are concerned.
This order shall not come in the way of acquiring the subject properties by issuing notification afresh, in accordance with law.
Added, liberty is also reserved to the respondent No.4-NICE to proceed against respondents No.1 to 3, in accordance with law if there is any grievance against them.

All contentions in that regard are kept open.
NC: 2023:KHC:28596 6.

However, learned Counsels for the respondent- KIADB as well as respondent-NICE, jointly submit that the compensation amount of about Rs.4,37,500/- has been released to the petitioner's vendors and therefore, the learned Counsels submit that a direction may be issued to the petitioner to return the said amount to KIADB, so that it can be credited/passed on to NICE.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits on instructions from the petitioner that the petitioner is ready and willing M/S Vijaya Properties vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198852628/
3 to redeposit the said amount with KIADB and the same shall be done within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Ordered accordingly.
No orders as to costs.
Pending I.As., if any, stand disposed of.
